subject: Request: SLA Exception & Latency Commitments for Private VPC Deployment
messages:
From: Jane Park <jane.park@acadiahealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom LeBlanc <tom.leblanc@acadiahealth.com>, procurement@acadiahealth.com
Date: Mon, 08 Sep 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC SLA / latency commitments — Acadia request

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we evaluate Redwood Private in our VPC for clinical decisioning, our security and procurement teams have a couple of asks around SLAs.

High level: Acadia needs stronger uptime and tail-latency commitments for the private deployment running in our Azure VNet. We understand private deployments are typically customer-controlled, but we need an exception to the standard shared-responsibility wording for the following items:

- A minimum monthly uptime guarantee of 99.95% for the Redwood control plane endpoints that integrate with our VPC (health checks, model routing).
- P95 latency for simple text-gen API calls <= 120ms for requests routed within the same Azure region.
- Clear escalation path and 1-hour response SLA for Sev-1 incidents affecting production inference.
- Evidence requirements: audit logs, uptime reports, and synthetic monitoring checks for the past 90 days.

Attached is a short doc that summarizes the asks and our network topology. Can Redwood confirm which of these you can accept, and where you will require us to accept risk because of customer-managed networking?

Thanks,
Jane Park
Director, IT Sourcing
Acadia Health

---
Attachment: Acadia_SLA_Request_v1.pdf (PDF, 42KB)
Attachment: network_topology.png (PNG, 512KB)

-----Original Message-----
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Jane Park <jane.park@acadiahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Sep 2025 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private VPC SLA / latency commitments — Acadia request

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. I copied our security and solutions leads below so we can validate the specifics: Priya (security) and Priyom (solutions).

Short answer: we can accept a limited set of SLA exceptions for Private deployments, but they require precise language about the customer-controlled components. A few quick clarifications we need from Acadia to map the responsibilities:

1) Which subnet/services will host the inference nodes vs. the control-plane connectors?
2) Will you be using our sidecar connector or peered private endpoints?
3) Do you have an existing APM/synthetic monitor we can consume (read-only) or shall Redwood deploy a small set of probe VMs?

I'll return with proposed clause language and an evidence package.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

-----Original Internal: 09 Sep 2025 09:23 - Redwood Internal Discussion -----
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Sep 2025 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC SLA / latency commitments — Acadia request

Team — forwarding Acadia's asks. Quick notes from solutions/security perspective:

- We can accept 99.95% monthly uptime for the Redwood-managed control plane endpoints if Acadia uses our managed private endpoint (Redwood-managed NIC and peering). If they insist on fully customer-hosted connectors (customer-managed VMs in their VNet with SSH access disabled to us), uptime becomes a composite metric we can't fully guarantee.
- On latency: 120ms P95 inside same region is achievable for small prompt paths on c5-like instances and a tuned kernel, but only if network egress through Azure stays within region and there are no cross-zone hops. We'll need their network diagram (they sent one) and a brief perf run.
- Sev-1 1-hour response is OK for our SOC-backed support team for control plane; for anything requiring access to customer-managed infra, we can commit to response/triage times, but remediation windows may be governed by customer's change window.

Action items: Rafael to confirm connector topology and whether Acadia will accept Redwood-managed private endpoint. Priya to prepare an evidence pack (logs, uptime history for similar customers) and a short proposed SLA addendum. Markus to flag any legal redlines (availability of remedies / credits). Monica to propose instrumentation options (synthetic probes).

- Priyom

-----Internal Legal Note: 10 Sep 2025 11:40 - Markus Klein -----
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC SLA / latency commitments — Acadia request

We should be cautious about credit formulas tied to customer-managed networking. Proposed approach: add an SLA addendum that differentiates "Redwood-managed components" and "Customer-managed components." For the former we can provide uptime and latency commitments plus credits. For the latter, we provide response/triage SLAs and a best-effort remediation, plus instrumentation requirements (synthetic checks and shared read-only logs).

Proposed clause (summary):
- Redwood warrants 99.95% uptime for Redwood-managed control-plane endpoints and will provide monthly uptime reports.
- For customer-managed connector components, Redwood will provide triage and escalation with defined response times but not uptime credits.
- Both parties agree to a joint monitoring configuration to enable attribution for outages (synthetic checks, timestamps, tracer IDs).

If Acadia insists on credits that apply across both sides, we need a higher price or an explicit runbook with dedicated managed endpoint.

- Markus

-----Public Reply to Customer: 12 Sep 2025 15:12 - Rafael Mendes -----
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Jane Park <jane.park@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, Tom LeBlanc <tom.leblanc@acadiahealth.com>, procurement@acadiahealth.com
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private VPC SLA / latency commitments — Acadia request

Hi Jane,

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed this internally. Below is a concise proposal designed to map responsibilities cleanly while meeting Acadia's compliance needs.

Summary of what Redwood can commit to (if Acadia accepts the deployment topology in Option A below):

1) Uptime: 99.95% monthly uptime guarantee for Redwood-managed control-plane endpoints (routing, model registry API, health-check endpoints). Monthly uptime reports will be provided within 5 business days of month end.

2) Latency: P95 tail latency of <=120ms for single-turn text-generation requests where: (a) requests originate from the same Azure region; (b) Acadia uses Redwood-managed private endpoint or Azure Private Link peering managed by Redwood; (c) requests do not exceed 1k tokens and do not trigger model fallback. Exceptions tied to abnormal network conditions or cross-region routing will be excluded.

3) Incident response: For Sev-1 production inference outages affecting Redwood-managed components, Redwood will acknowledge within 15 minutes and begin remediation/triage within 1 hour. If an outage requires access to customer-managed infrastructure, Redwood will escalate and coordinate with Acadia's on-call but will be limited to response/triage until access/permissions are granted.

4) Evidence and monitoring: Redwood will provide read-only access to synthetic probe dashboards, monthly uptime reports, and preserved audit logs for the control plane for 90 days. We will also agree to a joint instrumentation plan (synthetic checks and tracer IDs) to enable attribution.

Option A (preferred): Acadia accepts Redwood-managed private endpoint (Redwood deploys and manages the peered endpoint in your VNet). This enables full uptime and latency commitments and credit eligibility.

Option B (customer-hosted connector): Redwood provides response/triage SLAs, monthly reports, and instrumentation, but cannot provide uptime credits or guaranteed P95 latency. Any credits/financial remedies tied to outages affecting customer-hosted components will be disallowed in the base price; we can offer a priced managed connector add-on.

Attached is a draft SLA addendum with redline language for the contract team. Please let us know which option you prefer and any additional clarifications you need on the evidence pack. If Option A works, Monica can schedule a short network perf run next week.

Next steps:
- Jane: confirm preferred topology (Option A vs Option B) and availability for a 30-minute perf window.
- Procurement: if Option A, we'll deliver a short priced addendum for the managed endpoint.

Thanks and happy to hop on a call to walk through the wording.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
